doc.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Career, market and the state of jazz
title: Attention spans and the listening audience
summary: Rowe asks about media saturation and audiences; Jang muses on speed and Ellington/Mingus meter changes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What’s the effect of 80 cable channels, and constant music everywhere you go, on people’s attention span?

Boy. I wonder if the music’s going to sound like that. I mean like how Duke Ellington and Charles Mingus, you know they would change from meter to meter and tempo modulations, it would sound like, on what 78 or 156 on a turntable? You just speed it up. God I don’t know how that would — because you know in our social action now people are driving faster, spaces are becoming tighter.
I guess I was just wondering, the work you do, to me, requires a fairly sophisticated listening audience. And I worry that we still have that as time goes by.
